'''Monté Robert Morris''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|m|ɒ|n|t|eɪ}} {{respell|MON|tay}};<ref>{{cite press release|title=2023-24 start of season NBA pronunciation guide|url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-24-start-of-season-nba-pronunciation-guide|website=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2023|access-date=May 17, 2024}}</ref> born June 27, 1995) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]] of the [[Greek Basketball League]] (GBL) and the [[EuroLeague]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State Cyclones]].

==Early life==
Morris was born in Grand Rapids, Michigan and his mother is Latonia Morris. His mother nicknamed him "Man-Man" when he was born.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/collegebasketballnation/post/_/id/100285/iowa-states-morris-no-longer-little-man-man|title=Monte Morris no longer little Man-Man|date=September 25, 2014|website=ESPN.com|access-date=March 4, 2022}}</ref> He grew up in [[Flint, Michigan]] attending Flint Beecher High School. Morris was childhood friends with future NBA player and later NBA teammate, [[Kyle Kuzma]], as both attended Dailey Elementary School.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://sports.yahoo.com/childhood-friends-kyle-kuzma-and-monte-morris-finally-playing-together-in-nba-185702052.html | title=NBA free agency 2022: Childhood friends Kyle Kuzma and Monte Morris finally playing together in NBA }}</ref> He was a four-year starter for the Beecher Buccaneers. Morris was a three-time winner of Michigan's [[Associated Press]] Class C Player of the Year Award and a three time all-state selection.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mlive.com/highschoolsports/article/flint-beechers-monte-morris-named-ap-class-c-all-state-player-of-the-year/|title=Flint Beecher's Monte Morris named AP Class C All-State Player of the Year|agency=Associated Press|date=March 20, 2013|website=Mlive.com|access-date=March 4, 2022}}</ref> He led the Buccaneers in scoring, assists, and steals in all four seasons. He led Flint Beecher to back-to-back Class C Michigan state titles in 2012 and 2013. One of the nation's best point guards, Morris won [[Mr. Basketball of Michigan|Michigan's Mr. Basketball]] award in 2013.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mlive.com/highschoolsports/article/beecher-senior-monte-morris-wins-2013-mr-basketball-award-over-stellar-field-of-finalists-with-video/|title=Beecher senior Monte Morris wins 2013 Mr. Basketball award over stellar field of finalists (with video)|date=March 18, 2013|website=Mlive.com|access-date=March 4, 2022}}</ref>

He was ranked No. 96<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/recruiting/player-Monte-Morris-112003 |title=Monte Morris - Yahoo! Sports |access-date=January 14, 2017 |archive-date=July 9, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150709120035/http://sports.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/recruiting/player-Monte-Morris-112003 |url-status=dead }}</ref> in the final [[Rivals.com]] national rankings and No. 89 in the [[Scout.com]] ratings as well as being a [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://communitytable.com/14852/brianmclaughlin/meet-parades-2013-all-america-basketball-teams/|title=Meet PARADE's 2013 All-America Basketball Teams|first=Brian|last=McLaughlin|website=Communitytable.com|date=May 18, 2013 }}</ref> Morris was recruited to [[Butler Bulldogs men's basketball|Butler]], [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]], [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]], [[Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball|Arizona State]], [[Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball|Cincinnati]], [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]], [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]], and [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]] which he ultimately committed to.

==College career==
===Freshman season===
Morris started the season on the bench but worked his way into the starting line-up against the [[Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball|Oklahoma Sooners]] on February 1, 2014, staying there ever since. Morris averaged 6.8 points, 3.7 assists, and 2.6 rebounds and dished out 134 assists, the third most by any freshman in school history. He shot 84.7 percent (61–72) at the free-throw line, the second-best mark by an ISU freshman, and was the only Big 12 freshman to make at least 25 threes (28–69) and shoot over 40 percent. He scored double figures in 13 games, including all three games in the [[2014 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|NCAA tournament]]. Morris tallied a season-high 15 points in the Cyclones' NCAA Tournament win against [[North Carolina Central Eagles men's basketball|NCCU]] and followed that with 13 against the [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina Tar Heels]]. He dished out five or more assists in 12 games and led all Big 12 freshmen with 46 steals, the fifth most by an ISU rookie. His 1.3 steals per game ranked seventh in the Big 12, and he had an ISU freshman record of 12 assists with no turnovers against West Virginia. He played 52 minutes of turnover-free basketball in ISU's triple-OT win at [[Oklahoma State Cowboys men's basketball|Oklahoma State]] and had 10 points and five assists, including the game-winning 3-pointer with 43 seconds left in the third overtime against the Cowboys. He broke the NCAA record and led the nation with a 4.79 assist-to-turnover ratio, including a 6.9 assist-to-turnover ratio in Big 12 play.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://amestrib.com/sports/men-s-basketball-morris-goes-overshadowed-budding-star|title=Men's Basketball: Morris goes from overshadowed to budding star|website=Amestrib.com|access-date=March 4, 2022}}</ref>

===Sophomore season===
[[File:Big 12 Championship (25146155163).jpg|thumb|Morris in 2016]]
Morris started all 34 games and averaged 11.9 points, second on the team. He also posted a Big 12-best 5.2 assists and 3.4 rebounds on his way to earning All-Big 12 Second-Team honors. He had second-most assists of any sophomore and 11th-most by any player in school history. Morris was second in the Big 12 in field goal percentage shooting 50.7 percent from the field, had 64 steals, the second-most by a sophomore and tied for the ninth-most by any player in a single season in school history. His 110 steals in the last two seasons were the most by any Big 12 player. His first-career 20-point game came against [[Texas Tech Red Raiders men's basketball|Texas Tech]], he recorded his first double-double and just missed a triple-double with 11 points, 10 assists and seven rebounds against [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://amestrib.com/sports/men-s-basketball-cyclones-power-way-past-jayhawks|title=Men's Basketball: Cyclones power way past Jayhawks|website=Amestrib.com|access-date=March 4, 2022}}</ref> He tallied a career-high 24 points and hit a buzzer-beating 17-foot fadeaway to beat [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]] in Big 12 quarterfinals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2015/03/12/iowa-state-beats-texas-monte-morris-big-12-tournament|title=Watch: Monte Morris buzzer-beater lifts Iowa State over Texas in Big 12 tournament|website=Si.com}}</ref> He averaged 15.3 points to earn Big 12 All-Tournament team honors as the [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Cyclones]] won the [[Big 12 men's basketball tournament|Big 12 tournament]] for the second consecutive season and he did not commit a turnover in three games at the [[Big 12 men's basketball tournament|Big 12 Championship]]. He led the nation for the second consecutive season with a 4.63 assist-to-turnover ratio and finished season with 176 assists and just 38 turnovers.

===Junior season===
On February 1, 2016, he was named one of 10 finalists for the Bob Cousy Point Guard of the Year Award.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Nortlander|first1=Matt|title=Cat Barber, Fred VanVleet missing from list of Cousy Award finalists|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/25468790/cat-barber-fred-vanvleet-conspicuously-missing-from-cousy-award-finalists|access-date=February 2, 2016|work=[[CBS Sports]]|date=February 1, 2016}}</ref> He was named to the 35-man midseason watchlist for the [[Naismith College Player of the Year|Naismith Trophy]] on February 11.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Payne|first1=Terrence|title=Naismith Trophy midseason list announced|url=http://www.foxsports.com/college-basketball/story/oklahoma-sooners-buddy-hield-lsu-tigers-ben-simmons-naismith-trophy-35-finalists-021116|access-date=February 19, 2016|work=[[Fox Sports]]|date=February 11, 2016}}</ref>

===Senior season===
[[File:ISU vs Nevada (33115136630).jpg|thumb|left|Morris competing against Nevada in the NCAA tournament]]
Morris received preseason recognition on November 2, 2016, as the [[Associated Press]] named him to the preseason [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] team.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.foxsports.com/college-basketball/story/duke-s-allen-leads-ap-preseason-all-america-team-110216 |title=Duke's Allen leads AP preseason All-America team |work=[[Foxsports.com]] |date=November 2, 2016 |access-date=November 12, 2016}}</ref> At the end of his senior season, Morris broke the NCAA record assist-to-turnover ratio from 4.79 he set his freshman year to the new record of 5.21.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.freep.com/story/sports/nba/pistons/2017/06/23/2017-nba-draft-local-michigan-high-school-stars/422619001/|title=2017 NBA draft: Four Michigan prep stars go; U-M's Walton, CMU's Keene denied|access-date=June 23, 2017|date=June 23, 2017|work=[[Detroit Free Press]]|author=Crawford, Kirkland}}</ref> In 2017, Morris led Iowa State to a 5th seed in the NCAA tournament and got into the second round before losing to Purdue.

==Professional career==

===Denver Nuggets (2017–2022)===
Morris was selected in the second round, 51st pick overall by the [[Denver Nuggets]] in the [[2017 NBA draft]]. Following the [[NBA Summer League|Summer League]] he signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Nuggets. Under the terms of the deal he would split time between the Nuggets and a G League team that would be best designated for him.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/morris-signed |title=Nuggets Sign Rookie Monte Morris to Two-Way Contract |work=NBA.com |date=July 21, 2017 |access-date=July 21, 2017}}</ref> For Morris, he was assigned to the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] of the [[NBA G League]] on October 23, 2017.<ref>{{cite news|title=Denver Nuggets Assign Lydon/Transfer Craig, Morris to G League |url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/assign-lydon-transfer-craig-morris-102317 |access-date=October 23, 2017|work=NBA.com|date=October 23, 2017}}</ref> On December 12, 2017, Morris made his NBA debut against the [[Detroit Pistons]]. He recorded an assist in three minutes of action. In three games with the Nuggets, he averaged 3.3 points per game. Morris averaged 18.0 points, 4.5 rebounds, and 6.6 assists per game with Rio Grande Valley.<ref>{{cite news|title=Final 2017-18 NBA G League stats for ex-Iowa collegians|url=http://www.thegazette.com/final-nba-g-league-stats-for-ex-iowa-collegians-20180327|access-date=May 21, 2018|work=[[The Gazette (Cedar Rapids)|The Gazette]]|date=March 27, 2018}}</ref> Following the season, Morris would sign a three-year, $4.7 million standard contract.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 25, 2018 |title=Nuggets Sign Monte Morris To Three-Year Deal |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2018/07/nuggets-monte-morris-agree-to-three-year-deal.html |access-date=2026-05-03 |website=Hoopsrumors.com |language=en}}</ref>

On December 9, 2020, Morris signed a three-year, $27 million extension through the 2023–24 season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 7, 2020 |title=Denver Nuggets, Monte Morris agree to 3-year, $27M extension |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/30472484/denver-nuggets-monte-morris-agree-3-year-27m-extension |access-date=2026-05-03 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

On December 29, 2020, Morris scored a career-high 24 points in a 125–115 loss to the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/preview/_/gameId/401267215|title=Nuggets vs. Kings - Game Preview - December 29, 2020 - ESPN|website=ESPN.com|access-date=March 4, 2022}}</ref>

On February 16, 2022, Morris scored 13 points, including a game-winning three-point shot as time expired, in a 117–116 win over the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.denverpost.com/2022/02/17/monte-morris-buzzer-beating-nuggets-beat-warriors/|title=Inside Nuggets' Monte Morris' buzzer-beating 3-pointer vs. Warriors: "That's his nickname, Big Game Tae"|website=Denverpost.com|date=February 17, 2022|access-date=March 4, 2022}}</ref>

===Washington Wizards (2022–2023)===
On July 6, 2022, Morris was traded, alongside [[Will Barton]], to the [[Washington Wizards]] in exchange for [[Kentavious Caldwell-Pope]] and [[Ish Smith]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-acquire-morris-and-barton-in-trade-with-denver/|title=Wizards Acquire Morris and Barton in Trade with Denver|website=nba.com|date=July 6, 2022|access-date=July 6, 2022}}</ref> Morris made his Wizards debut on October 19, recording seven points, six rebounds, six assists and two steals in a 114–107 win over the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=BEAL, WIZARDS OPEN SEASON WITH 114-107 WIN OVER PACERS |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022200004 |access-date=February 16, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

===Detroit Pistons (2023–2024)===
On July 6, 2023, Morris was traded to the [[Detroit Pistons]] in exchange for a future second-round pick.<ref>{{cite web|title=DETROIT PISTONS ACQUIRE MONTE MORRIS|url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-acquire-monte-morris|website=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2023|access-date=July 8, 2023}}</ref> Due to a lengthy recovery from a quadriceps injury to begin the 2023–24 season, Morris played in just six games for the Pistons before being dealt away at the NBA trade deadline.

===Minnesota Timberwolves (2024)===
On February 8, 2024, Morris was traded to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] in exchange for [[Troy Brown Jr.]], [[Shake Milton]] and a 2030 second-round pick.<ref>{{cite web|title=Minnesota Timberwolves Acquire Guard Monte Morris from Detroit Pistons|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/minnesota-timberwolves-acquire-guard-monte-morris-from-detroit-pistons|website=NBA.com|date=February 8, 2024|access-date=February 9, 2024}}</ref>

===Phoenix Suns (2024–2025)===
On July 5, 2024, Morris signed with the [[Phoenix Suns]] on a minimum deal.<ref>{{cite web|title=SUNS SIGN MONTE MORRIS|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/news/suns-sign-monte-morris|website=NBA.com|date=July 5, 2024|access-date=July 6, 2024}}</ref> He made 45 appearances for the Suns during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 5.2 points, 1.5 rebounds, and 1.6 assists.

===Indiana Pacers (2025)===
On September 23, 2025, Morris agreed to a contract with the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Pacers' Monte Morris: Signs with Indiana|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/pacers-monte-morris-signs-with-indiana/|access-date=November 6, 2025|website=cbssports.com|language=en}}</ref> However, two days later it was announced that the team would not sign Morris due to a calf strain.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Veteran Monte Morris Injures Calf, Will Not Sign With Pacers|url=https://www.si.com/nba/veteran-monte-morris-injures-calf-will-not-sign-with-pacers|access-date=November 6, 2025|website=si.com|language=en}}</ref> On November 6, Morris officially signed with the Pacers following the release of [[Mac McClung]].<ref>{{cite web | last=Sam | first=Doric | title=Mac McClung Reportedly Waived by Pacers, Monte Morris to Join Roster on New Contract | website=Bleacher Report | date=2025-11-06 | url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/25285739-mac-mcclung-reportedly-waived-pacers-monte-morris-join-roster-new-contract | access-date=2025-12-02}}</ref> Morris was waived by the Pacers on November 20.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-11-20 |title=Monte Morris: Waived by Indiana |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/monte-morris-waived-by-indiana/ |access-date=2025-11-20 |website=CBS Sports |language=en}}</ref>

===Olympiacos (2025–2026)===
On December 10, 2025, Morris signed with [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]] of the [[Greek Basketball League]] (GBL) and the [[EuroLeague]] until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-12-10 |title=Monte Morris joins Olympiacos
|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/euroleague/news/monte-morris-joins-olympiacos-bc/ |access-date=2025-12-10 |website=EuroLeague|language=en-US}}</ref> On July 2, 2026, the team officially announced they had parted ways with Morris.<ref>{{cite web |title=Olympiacos part ways with former NBA veteran |url=https://basketnews.com/news-251146-monte-morris-leaves-olympiacos.html |website=basketnews.com |access-date=14 July 2026 |language=en}}</ref>

==National team career==
On March 20, 2021, Morris committed to play for the [[Nigeria men's national basketball team|Nigerian national team]] as a naturalized player.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/31097946/denver-nuggets-morris-commits-play-nigeria-internationally|title=Denver Nuggets' Monte Morris commits to play for Nigeria internationally|work=ESPN|author=Colin Udoh|date=March 20, 2021|access-date=May 21, 2021}}</ref>
